answer: kappa is set by the smallest of the seven dominant margins in the cost accounting. Every dominant cost, divided by V = Tp = Theta(n), is a power p^(1-g_i) of p with margin g_i. The smallest margin is g_2 for chunk exchanges, whose cost per unit volume is p K^(tau-1) with K = Theta(p^(epsilon c)), so g_2 = epsilon c (1 - tau) = 2^-75 * 2^-56 * 2^-50 = 2^-181. Because K^(tau-1) = p^(-epsilon c (1-tau)), the margin is fixed by the axis-count exponent epsilon, the chunk-width exponent c and the interchange saving 1 - tau. The margin is taken to be twice kappa because every dominant term is at most p^(1-2 kappa), and the leftover fixed powers of log p are at most p^kappa for large p, so the total is p^(1-kappa), i.e. O(n (lg n)^(1-kappa)). With margin kappa alone the bound would be p^1 and there would be no saving. Since g_2 = 2^-181 = 2 kappa, kappa = 2^-182 is the largest power-of-two value the margin allows. The wiki states kappa = 2^-182 as a fixed choice; it does not derive that value.

stuck.note: This sentence is garbled: it has no full stop, and it joins the small-n case to the claim for every n >= 1 without a clear step. I could not tell whether it is a claim or a remark, and so could not tell whether the bound is established for all n or only for large n.

The page only says that some tau with s/W < m^tau is chosen, and that tau is close to 1. The page does not say why tau = 1 - 2^-50 specifically. That value appears only on the parameter page, where it is a fixed choice, so I could not tell whether it is a derived value or a chosen one.

The page fixes kappa = 2^-182 and calls it conservative, but does not say what conservative means or why the value is half the chunk-exchange margin and not some other value. I worked out for myself that 2 kappa must be at most 2^-181, so kappa <= 2^-182, and that 2^-182 is the largest power of two that fits. The wiki itself does not state this reasoning.

reason: I am fairly sure of the arithmetic: the chunk-exchange margin g_2 = epsilon c (1 - tau) = 2^-181 is the smallest of the seven margins, and kappa = 2^-182 is half of it. I am less sure of the factor 2, because the wiki's step from the powers to p^kappa depends on fixed powers of log p that I could not locate on any page I opened. I used 8 pages (the front page (home), the cost page (vor), the parameter page (fef), the interchange page (pid), the conjecture page (kaf), the main result page (nut), the page with handle siz, and the tape layout page with handle mov) plus one search for 'margin'.
